newsitem.title: SPAIN: POLL-Bank of Spain seen holding rate until mid-May.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Bank of Spain seen holding rate until mid-May.

text.p: The Bank of Spain will not reduce its key 5.50 percent money market rate on Wednesday, having already cut the rate three times this year with the last move a week-ago, analysts said on Tuesday.
Of eleven analysts and market dealers polled by Reuters Tuesday, not one was expecting a cut tomorrow.

But odds remain in favour of further falls in the official rate, with another 25-basis-point cut expected as soon as mid-May, after the announcement of what is expected to be a benign April consumer price index, the survey showed.

"They can cut the rate as soon as May 16, after the April CPI release and before the U.S. Federal Reserve Federal Open Market Committee meeting," said Alfredo Urrutia, chief economist at Societe Generale in Madrid.
But others were suggesting the central bank might adopt a slower, more cautious approach.
"We're more cautious. We expect a cut before the end of the second quarter," said Heather Richardson, London UBS economist.
For some, the Bank of Spain is reaching the end of its cuts and may not parcel the next one out for a couple months.

"We think they are close to the bottom. It's possible that they will cut by another 25 basis points by June and then keep their rate steady from there," said Francesco Giordano, economist at Credit Suisse First Boston in London.

The Bank of America in Madrid, which forecast CPI would fall to a low in May of 1.7 percent year-on-year, said that the Bank of Spain still has scope of 50 basis points for further cuts this year. It expects the Bank of Spain to cut as soon as April, leaving itself a margin of an additional 25 basis points.
The Bank of Spain last cut rates by 25 basis points on April 15 to 5.5 percent.
